rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable orthostatic hypotension after collapse/falls; Diagnose probable hyperventilation after collapse/falls; Diagnose probable common faint after collapse/falls
rule_level_problems.problem: The flowchart's first decision is 'systolic drop ≥ 20 OR diastolic drop ≥ 10'. All three rules test only the systolic reduction. A patient with a diastolic postural drop ≥ 10 and systolic drop < 20 is wrongly routed down the No branch and can be diagnosed with probable hyperventilation or common faint instead of orthostatic hypotension. No 'reduction in diastolic BP on standing' observable exists in SNOMED and the language cannot compute a difference, so the fix is either a documented not_representable note or a fallback: check for 'Postural drop in blood pressure' (finding, 271648003) and use it as an alternative Yes condition / a (no ...) in the No branch.

'(clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Vaccination given" "situation"))' has no temporal restriction. The page's criterion is collapse following vaccination; as encoded, any recorded vaccination history makes every collapse or fall Urgent. Add a Recent qualifier (consistent with 'Traumatic injury' + Recent in the same rule) or an onset comparison.

The page defines 'shock likely' in footnote 2 (SBP < 80, pulse ≥ 100, RR > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness). Per the house standard an 'X likely' becomes a probable diagnosis rule and the priority rule references (active_condition X). Only the SBP < 80 part is in the priority rule; the rest of the definition is absent and shock is otherwise left to free recording.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable hyperventilation after collapse/falls; Diagnose probable common faint after collapse/falls
rule_level_problems.problem: Both rules require '(< (measurement "Level of reduction in systolic blood pressure on standing") 20)', so neither fires until the lying/standing BP has actually been measured and the derived reduction recorded. This is faithful to the flowchart, but if the derived observable is not something the system records (the measure task lists it, so it may be fine), the two probable diagnoses can never be reached. Worth confirming that a derived 'reduction' measurement is recordable rather than only the four raw readings.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose possible anaphylaxis after sudden collapse; Urgent: collapse/falls with danger signs
rule_level_problems.problem: The anaphylaxis branch is gated on 'Collapse' with the 'Sudden onset' qualifier, a different piece of evidence from the plain 'Collapse' warning sign that triggers the page. The qualified form is in the check_for so it can be recorded, but a nurse who records plain Collapse plus wheeze/face swelling will not trigger the possible Anaphylaxis diagnosis (and the page-28 check task it is meant to reach). Consider accepting plain Collapse here, since the page's presenting complaint is already 'has collapsed'.
Footnote 1 limits allergen exposure to 'within the past few hours'; the exposure findings carry no time window. Low weight, as page 20 (gold) also omits it.

summary: The red box is encoded almost completely and accurately: 17 of 18 criteria are correct, with the one error being 'Vaccination given' with no temporal restriction, which makes any vaccination history an urgent trigger. The most consequential problem is in the flowchart: the orthostatic hypotension decision tests only systolic drop ≥ 20 and ignores the page's 'or diastolic drop ≥ 10', so diastolic-only postural drops are misrouted to the hyperventilation/common faint branch. Footnote 2's definition of 'shock likely' is not encoded as a probable Shock rule, leaving the red box's 'Shock' criterion dependent on free recording.
